HISTORY AND PHYSICAL (H&P) NOTE

Patient: Sarah Smith DOB: 02-Nov-1992 Encounter: Telehealth (Dr. Dean) Date: [today’s date]

History:
• Presenting complaint: 7-day history of persistent fever with alternating chills/night sweats.  
• Associated symptoms: Generalized myalgia, marked fatigue, nausea with ↓ oral intake, mild baseline headaches only.  
• Denies: Cough, sore throat, ear pain, diarrhea, neck stiffness, photophobia, rash, joint swelling, dysuria, urinary frequency/urgency.  
• Recent travel: Returned from Vietnam 4 weeks ago; extensive rural trekking/cycling; daily malaria prophylaxis taken (drug name unknown).  
• Self-care: Regular OTC paracetamol and ibuprofen (recommended doses) with only partial relief.

Past Medical History:
• Chronic mechanical back pain (under physiotherapy).  
• Allergic rhinitis (pollen).  
• No previous major illnesses or hospitalizations documented.  
Family history: Father died of myocardial infarction at age 68.  
Medications:  
  – Seroxat (paroxetine)—dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  – PRN ibuprofen and paracetamol (OTC).  
Allergies: No drug allergies reported; seasonal pollen allergy only.  
Social: Non-smoker; moderate alcohol; works as a nurse; engages in moderate exercise; vaccinations (incl. Hep B) up to date.

Physical Examination:
• Teleconsultation—no direct exam performed.  
• Patient reports fever, diaphoresis, and fatigue but no focal localizing signs.  
• Mentation: Conversational, coherent.  
• Negative symptom review as above (no rash, neck stiffness, respiratory, GI, or urinary focal signs).

Impression:
Fever of unknown origin post-travel; rule out malaria or other tropical/latent infections.

Management Plan:
1. Arrange same-day in-person evaluation at central London clinic (or local A&E if more convenient).  
2. Proposed investigations (to be ordered after exam):  
   • Thick and thin blood films for malaria.  
   • Full blood count, CRP/ESR, urea & electrolytes, LFTs.  
   • Additional cultures/tests per clinical findings.  
3. Advise patient to refrain from work until evaluation completed.  
4. Administrative team to contact patient and schedule clinic slot; patient to call provided number within minutes of this visit.  
5. Document clinician’s assessment and investigation requests in notes for receiving team.

Patient Summary:
26-year-old nurse with a week of undifferentiated fever, myalgia, and night sweats shortly after travel to rural Vietnam. No clear infective focus; malaria or other tropical infection must be excluded. She will attend clinic today for examination and targeted blood tests.

Key Takeaways:
• Attend the clinic (or A&E) today for physical exam and blood tests, including malaria screen.  
• Do not return to work until the cause of the fever is clarified.  
• Call the provided number immediately after this call to secure appointment time.

Next Steps:
• Perform full physical exam and initial labs today.  
• Manage per results—consider admission if unstable or positive malaria smear.  
• Follow-up contact once results available; provide fit note if needed.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing/expected elements: Vital signs, detailed medication doses, full allergy list, physical exam findings—pending in-person visit.  
• Internal conflicts: None noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear; minimal background noise; no major inaudible segments.
